beats.intro: Multiplying and dividing decimals uses the same steps as whole numbers. [[q]]The only new question is where the decimal point goes.
beats.grid: What is zero point three times zero point four? [[sq]]Here's one whole, cut into a hundred small squares. [[a]]Shade three tenths across. [[b]]Now shade four tenths down. [[both]]The part shaded both ways is three rows of four squares: twelve small squares. [[ans]]Each small square is one hundredth, so the product is twelve hundredths, zero point one two. [[why]]Tenths times tenths make hundredths. That's why the decimal places add up.
beats.rule: So here's the method. [[q]]Five point three two times one point four. [[s1]]No negative signs, so the answer is positive. [[s2]]Multiply as if there were no decimal points: five hundred thirty-two times fourteen is seven thousand four hundred forty-eight. [[s3]]Count the decimal places in the factors: two in five point three two, and one in one point four. That's three in all. [[hop]]Start at the right end and move the decimal point three places to the left. [[ans]]Seven point four four eight. [[check]]Check with an estimate: five times one and a half is about seven. It fits.
beats.zeros: Now three point one two times negative zero point five. [[s1]]One negative sign, so the answer is negative. [[s2]]Three hundred twelve times five is one thousand five hundred sixty. [[s3]]There are three decimal places in all, [[hop]]so the product is negative one point five six zero. [[drop]]A zero at the end of the decimal part doesn't change the value, so write negative one point five six.
beats.q1: Quick check. Where does the decimal point go?
beats.divMeaning: Now division. [[q]]What is two point eight divided by zero point seven? [[ask]]It asks how many zero point sevens fit in two point eight. [[bar]]Here are two point eight wholes, cut into tenths: twenty-eight tenths. [[group]]Group them seven tenths at a time. [[count]]Four groups. [[same]]And twenty-eight divided by seven is also four.
beats.scale: That's the trick for dividing. [[pat]]Six divided by two, sixty divided by twenty, and six hundred divided by two hundred all equal three. [[rule]]Multiplying both numbers by the same ten, hundred, or thousand doesn't change the quotient. [[ex]]For negative six point nine one two divided by zero point zero three, [[sign]]one negative sign: the answer is negative. [[hop]]Multiply both by a hundred, so the divisor becomes the whole number three. [[div]]Six hundred ninety-one point two divided by three is two hundred thirty point four. [[ans]]So the answer is negative two hundred thirty point four.
beats.q2: Quick check. Make the divisor a whole number, then divide.
beats.story: A cyclist rides thirty-two point six four kilometers in two point four hours. [[q]]How far does she ride each hour, at the same pace? [[expr]]Divide the distance by the time. [[hop]]Multiply both by ten: three hundred twenty-six point four divided by twenty-four. [[ans]]That's thirteen point six kilometers each hour. [[see]]Each hour on the time line matches thirteen point six kilometers on the distance line.
beats.q3: Quick check. A division that needs rounding.
beats.wrap: To multiply decimals, [[w1]]multiply as whole numbers, then count the decimal places in both factors to place the point. [[w2]]To divide, multiply both numbers by the same power of ten until the divisor is a whole number. [[w3]]Use the sign rules you know, and check with an estimate. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
